clauses.current_legal_basis: Established original_plus_bounded_search route: the order's own held original text (28 FR 819) read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog; every held later instrument (EO 11382 section 13, EO 12608 section 15, EO 13286 section 69) attached as an event; no revocation, supersession or own-terms end held. Corroboration (not a claim source, because only the extracted note text, not the Code bytes, is held): the current-law note extract printed under 10 U.S.C. 2603 prints the designation as amended by those three orders with no ending statement, and shows the section 2603 named as authority still in the Code.
clauses.reason: The designation continues as amended. EO 11382 section 13 (signed 1967-11-28; no separate effective-date clause) replaced the Secretary of the Treasury with the Secretary of Transportation; EO 12608 section 15 (signed 1987-09-09, no effective-date clause) replaced the Department and Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare with the Department and Secretary of Health and Human Services in the listed orders including 11079; EO 13286 section 69 replaced the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security effective 2003-03-01 (section 92 of EO 13286: "This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003."). The held current-law note extract prints the designation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

research_rationale:
EO 11079 (28 FR 819, signed 1963-01-25; held official Federal Register text, page location high) is a single designation made under section 2603 of title 10, United States Code: the Secretary of Defense (Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps members), the Secretary of the Treasury (Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy) and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (commissioned officers of the Public Health Service) are to prescribe regulations under which members may accept fellowships, scholarships or grants, uniform so far as practicable. The held original has no sunset, expiry, condition or revocation. Three later orders changed the officers named: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation), EO 12608 section 15 (1987-09-09; Health, Education, and Welfare to Health and Human Services) and EO 13286 section 69 (effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security). None revokes or supersedes the order. The held current-law extract of the Code (only the extracted note text is held, so it is corroboration and not a claim source) prints the order as amended by all three as a note to 10 U.S.C. 2603, so the authority section named in the order is still in the Code, and the note carries no ending statement. The ofr_catalog search reports three hits for this order, which are the three amendments. Cutoff limit: the held Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected.
